title: Deem Not That They Are Blest Alone
description: Deem Not That They Are Blest Alone in Tonic Solfa to MELCOMBE, doh is Eb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: William Cullen Bryant wrote these words. They were printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 326, “Blessed Are They That Mourn”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre (8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to MELCOMBE; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Deem not that they are blest a-lone Whose days a peace-ful te-nor keep; The God who loves our race has shown A bless-ing for the eyes that weep.

lines: Deem not that they are blest alone
Whose days a peaceful tenor keep;
The God who loves our race has shown
A blessing for the eyes that weep.
The light of smiles shall fill again
The lids that now o'erflow with tears,
And weary hours of woe and pain
O, there are days of hope and rest
For every dark and troubled night!
And grief may bide, an evening guest,
But joy shall come with morning light.
And ye, who o'er a friend's low bier
Now shed the bitter drops like rain,
Know that a brighter, happier sphere
Will give him to your arms again.

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: William Cullen Bryant died in 1878.
credits: Words by William Cullen Bryant (1794–1878), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to MELCOMBE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
